title: Laredo man sentenced to more than six years in prison in human smuggling case
excerpt: Javier Zamora, of Laredo, was sentenced to more than six years in federal prison after pleading guilty to transporting a person in the country illegally for money. Prosecutors say he drove up to 140 mph before his vehicle caught fire, then struggled with an officer over a gun.
content:
A Laredo man was sentenced to more than six years in federal prison in a human smuggling case that ended with a high-speed chase, a burning vehicle, and a struggle over an officer's gun.

Javier Zamora pleaded guilty to transporting a person in the country illegally for money. Court records show he had a previous federal conviction for human smuggling.

Prosecutors say Zamora drove up to 140 mph through Laredo before his vehicle caught fire. He then ran toward a ranch, and when an officer caught up with him, Zamora grabbed the officer's arm while the officer was holding a gun. The gun went off during the struggle, and the officer was hurt.

Zamora's attorney declined to comment.
